title: Retraction-corrected primitive assembly and pointwise finite uniform summation
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a normed $\mathbf Q_\ell$-vector space $V$, not necessarily complete, with $\|v+w\|\leq\max(\|v\|,\|w\|)$ and $\|av\|=|a|_\ell\|v\|$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Let $S$ be a nonempty profinite space, $G$ a profinite group, and $n\geq2$. Here profinite means compact Hausdorff totally disconnected, and group operations are continuous. Define $C_V^r=C(S\times G^r,V)$, with trivial action, $d^0=0$, and
$$(dh)(s;g_1,\ldots,g_{r+1})=h(s;g_2,\ldots,g_{r+1})+\sum_{a=1}^r(-1)^ah(s;g_1,\ldots,g_ag_{a+1},\ldots,g_{r+1})+(-1)^{r+1}h(s;g_1,\ldots,g_r).$$
Let $(A_j)_{j\geq1}$ be nonempty closed subsets covering $S$, with continuous retractions $\rho_j:S\to A_j$, and locally constant maps $k_i:S\to\{1,\ldots,i\}$, $i\geq1$, eventually equal at each $s$ to $j(s)=\min\{j:s\in A_j\}$. For every $j$ let $T_j:C_V^n\to C_V^{n-1}$ be a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear operator given by
$$(T_j h)(s,x)=\sum_{a=1}^{u_j}\alpha_{j,a}h(s,\psi_{j,a}(x)),$$
where the sum is finite, $\alpha_{j,a}\in\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $\psi_{j,a}:G^{n-1}\to G^n$ is continuous. Suppose $\|T_j h\|_\infty\leq C_j\|h\|_\infty$ with $C_j\geq1$; set $D_i=\max(1,C_1,\ldots,C_i)$. Let $e_i\in C_V^n$, $c_i\in C_V^{n-1}$, $i\geq0$, satisfy $de_i=0$, $dc_i=e_i$, and for $i\geq1$,
$$\max(\|e_i\|_\infty,\|c_i\|_\infty)\leq 2^{-(i-1)}/D_i.$$
Assume $e_i(s,y)=0$ eventually for every fixed $(s,y)$, the partial sums $\sum_{i=0}^Ne_i$ converge uniformly in $\widehat V$ to a continuous $z:S\times G^n\to V$, and
$$d(T_j e_i)(a,-)=e_i(a,-)\quad(a\in A_j,\ 1\leq j\leq i).$$
For $i\geq1$ and $1\leq j\leq i$, with $v_{i,j}=c_i-T_je_i$, define
$$B_{i,j}(s,x)=(T_je_i)(s,x)+v_{i,j}(s,x)-v_{i,j}(\rho_j(s),x),\quad b_0=c_0,\quad b_i(s,x)=B_{i,k_i(s)}(s,x)\ (i\geq1).$$
These $B_{i,j}$ and $b_i$ are continuous $V$-valued cochains; for $1\leq j\leq i$ one has $dB_{i,j}=e_i$ and $B_{i,j}(s,-)=T_je_i(s,-)$ for every $s\in A_j$. Moreover
$$\|B_{i,j}\|_\infty\leq\max(\|c_i\|_\infty,C_j\|e_i\|_\infty),\qquad db_i=e_i,\qquad \|b_i\|_\infty\leq2^{-(i-1)}\ (i\geq1).$$
For each fixed $(s,x)$, $b_i(s,x)=0$ for all sufficiently large $i$. The partial sums $\sum_{i=0}^Nb_i$ converge uniformly in the norm completion $\widehat V$, their limit takes values in $V$ and is continuous for its original norm topology, and this limit $b_*$ satisfies $db_*=z$ as an equality of actual cochains. Use [def-weil-size-convention].

proof.text: Write $R_jh(s,x)=h(\rho_j(s),x)$, viewing $\rho_j(s)$ in $S$. Since $\rho_j$ and the $\psi_{j,a}$ are continuous, the finite formula for $T_j$ and continuity of addition and scalar multiplication make $T_je_i$, $v_{i,j}$, $R_jv_{i,j}$ and $B_{i,j}$ continuous. The displayed differential changes only the group variables, so direct substitution in each of its finitely many terms gives $d(R_jh)=R_j(dh)$; it is also linear.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion of old primitive-descent proof steps 11–13; Q59 detailed proof step 1.

proof.text: Fix $i\geq1$ and $1\leq j\leq i$. The hypotheses give $dv_{i,j}=e_i-dT_je_i$, which is zero at every parameter in $A_j$. Since $\rho_j(s)\in A_j$, step 1 gives $d(R_jv_{i,j})=0$. Consequently $dB_{i,j}=dT_je_i+dv_{i,j}-dR_jv_{i,j}=e_i$. If $s\in A_j$, then $\rho_j(s)=s$, so the two $v_{i,j}$ terms cancel and $B_{i,j}(s,-)=T_je_i(s,-)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion of old primitive-descent proof steps 11–13; Q59 detailed proof step 2.

proof.text: Put $M_{i,j}=\max(\|c_i\|_\infty,C_j\|e_i\|_\infty)$. The ultrametric inequality and the assumed operator bound give $\|v_{i,j}(t,x)\|\leq M_{i,j}$ for every $(t,x)$. Rewrite $B_{i,j}=c_i-R_jv_{i,j}$; since $\rho_j(s)\in S$, its pointwise norm is at most $M_{i,j}$. Taking the supremum proves the claimed bound for $B_{i,j}$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion of old primitive-descent proof steps 11–13; Q59 detailed proof step 3.

proof.text: For fixed $i\geq1$, every $s$ has an open neighbourhood on which $k_i$ is the constant $j=k_i(s)$. On this neighbourhood times $G^{n-1}$, $b_i=B_{i,j}$, so $b_i$ is continuous. Every face in $d$ has the same parameter $s$, hence uses this same $j$; step 2 therefore gives $db_i=e_i$. Since $C_j\leq D_i$ and $D_i\geq1$, step 3 and the assumed smallness give $\|b_i\|_\infty\leq D_i\max(\|c_i\|_\infty,\|e_i\|_\infty)\leq2^{-(i-1)}$. Also $b_0=c_0$ is continuous and $db_0=e_0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion of old primitive-descent proof steps 11–13; Q59 detailed proof step 4.

proof.text: Fix $(s,x)$ and put $j=j(s)$. Eventually $i\geq j$ and $k_i(s)=j$; since $s\in A_j$, step 2 gives $b_i(s,x)=T_je_i(s,x)=\sum_{a=1}^{u_j}\alpha_{j,a}e_i(s,\psi_{j,a}(x))$. Here $j$, the coefficients and all evaluation points are fixed. For each of these finitely many points the hypothesis makes $e_i$ eventually zero. Take a common index for these thresholds and selector stabilization. Then $b_i(s,x)=0$ beyond it. The empty sum $u_j=0$ is already zero.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion of old primitive-descent proof steps 11–13; Q59 detailed proof step 5.

proof.text: Define $b_*(q)\in V$ to be the eventual constant value of $P_N(q)=\sum_{i=0}^Nb_i(q)$, which exists by step 5. For each $N\geq0$ and $q=(s,x)$ choose $M\geq N$ beyond the vanishing threshold at $q$. Then $b_*(q)-P_N(q)=\sum_{i=N+1}^{M}b_i(q)$. Repeated application of the ultrametric inequality and step 4 bounds this finite sum by $2^{-N}$, including when it is empty. The bound is independent of $q$ and tends to zero, proving uniform convergence directly in $V$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion of old primitive-descent proof steps 11–13; Q59 detailed proof step 6.

proof.text: Fix $q$ and $\varepsilon>0$, and choose $N$ with $2^{-N}<\varepsilon$. The finite sum $P_N$ is continuous, so on some neighbourhood of $q$, $\|P_N(q\prime)-P_N(q)\|<\varepsilon$. Step 6 and the ultrametric inequality yield $\|b_*(q\prime)-b_*(q)\|\leq\max(2^{-N},\|P_N(q\prime)-P_N(q)\|)<\varepsilon$. This proves continuity of $b_*$ for the original norm topology of $V$, with no completeness assumption.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion of old primitive-descent proof steps 11–13; Q59 detailed proof step 7.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-metric-completion-isometry] to the metric $d_V(v,w)=\|v-w\|$. For the canonical $\iota:V\to\widehat V$, step 6 gives $d_{\widehat V}(\iota P_N(q),\iota b_*(q))=\|P_N(q)-b_*(q)\|\leq2^{-N}$. Thus the same partial sums converge uniformly in the completion to $\iota b_*$. This identifies the completed limit with the actual $V$-valued continuous cochain constructed above.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion of old primitive-descent proof steps 11–13; Q59 detailed proof step 8.

proof.text: Fix $(s,y)\in S\times G^n$. The formula for $d$ uses finitely many points of $S\times G^{n-1}$. By step 5 choose a common threshold after which $P_N$ equals $b_*$ at every one of these points. Thus $db_*(s,y)=dP_N(s,y)=\sum_{i=0}^Ne_i(s,y)$ beyond that threshold, by linearity and step 4. For each $\varepsilon>0$, take such an $N$ also beyond the convergence threshold for the assumed completed series. The distance identity of [lem-sfb-metric-completion-isometry] gives $\|db_*(s,y)-z(s,y)\|=d_{\widehat V}(\iota\sum_{i=0}^Ne_i(s,y),\iota z(s,y))<\varepsilon$. The nonnegative norm is therefore zero, so $db_*(s,y)=z(s,y)$ in $V$.
